title: Model & Retrieval Supply Chains
description: Study dataset provenance and poisoning, model artifact integrity, dependency and tool provenance, and retrieval integrity and source ranking. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Dataset provenance and poisoning
lessons.description: Design deduplication and source-review checks for the batch.
lessons.conceptOverview: Record dataset sources, transformations and review history. Poisoning can target learned behavior or retrieval answers, so inspect changes and evaluate suspicious clusters rather than relying only on aggregate size.
lessons.whyItMatters: Repeated untrusted content can distort both training and retrieval.

lessons.title: Model artifact integrity
lessons.description: Describe an isolated review and approved-artifact process.
lessons.conceptOverview: Obtain model artifacts from identified sources, verify integrity where available and review loading behavior. Some serialization formats or custom code paths can execute code; treat unfamiliar artifacts as software dependencies.
lessons.whyItMatters: Model loading can involve software execution and needs supply-chain controls.

lessons.title: Dependency and tool provenance
lessons.description: Compare requested permissions with the task and define a minimal allowed scope.
lessons.conceptOverview: Pin and review dependencies, including plugins and tool servers. A narrow tool description does not prove its implementation only accesses the advertised resources.
lessons.whyItMatters: Dependency permissions should match required capabilities.

lessons.title: Retrieval integrity and source ranking
lessons.description: Design source validation and evidence checks before answering.
lessons.conceptOverview: Attackers may manipulate retrievable content or metadata to gain visibility. Preserve provenance, enforce source policies and evaluate whether high-ranked evidence actually supports the answer.
lessons.whyItMatters: Ranking position is not a trust guarantee.
